summary: All ten occurrences support kämpfen. Retain the glossary’s stem I designation and mḥawrable/mḥawrəb forms; do not relabel them Q or II solely because of quadriliteral shape or Arabic III ancestry.

Joint combatants may be a plural subject, overtly ele w lu kurrək, whereas an adversary with a single subject is expressed by ʕam-/aʕm-. The l-shaped coordinated phrases in 98/55 are joint agents, not simply a patient.
Preterit with a morning–sunset span can describe extended combat; a duration does not convert the form into another box. kəmḥawrabno with hani kmo yawme is ongoing activity with elapsed duration.
